title: Time, days, and making plans
goal: Tell the time with four special Urdu words — ساڑھے، سوا، پونے، ڈیڑھ — name the days and months, and arrange to meet.
bekal: say and ask what time it is
name the seven days of the week

dialogs.title: مکالمہ — ملنے کا وقت
dialogs.intro: Ayesha phones Budi to set a time to study together this weekend.

lines.speaker: عائشہ:
lines.text: ہیلو بودی! آپ اس ہفتے فارغ ہیں؟
lines.baca: hailo Būdī! āp is hafte fāriġ haiñ?
lines.id: Hello, Budi! Are you free this week?
lines.literal: hello Budi! you this week free are?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: جی، جمعرات کو فارغ ہوں۔ کیوں؟
lines.baca: jī, jumerāt ko fāriġ hūñ. kyūñ?
lines.id: Yes, I'm free on Thursday. Why?
lines.literal: yes, Thursday on free am. why?

lines.speaker: عائشہ:
lines.text: ہم مل کر اردو پڑھتے ہیں؟ لائبریری میں۔
lines.baca: ham mil kar urdū paṛhte haiñ? lāibrerī meñ.
lines.id: Shall we study Urdu together? At the library.
lines.literal: we having-met Urdu study are? library in.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: ساڑھے چار — یعنی چار بج کر تیس منٹ؟
lines.baca: sāṛhe chār — ya'nī chār baj kar tīs minaṭ?
lines.id: Half past four — you mean four thirty?
lines.literal: half-past four — that-is four having-struck thirty minutes?

lines.speaker: عائشہ:
lines.text: جی بالکل۔ چار بج کر تیس منٹ۔
lines.baca: jī bilkul. chār baj kar tīs minaṭ.
lines.literal: yes exactly. four having-struck thirty minutes.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: معاف کیجیے، مجھے یہ ابھی مشکل لگتا ہے۔
lines.baca: ma'āf kījiye, mujhe ye abhī mushkil lagtā hai.
lines.id: Sorry, I still find this hard.
lines.literal: pardon do-please, to-me this now difficult seems.

lines.speaker: عائشہ:
lines.text: کوئی بات نہیں! لائبریری کب بند ہوتی ہے؟
lines.baca: koī bāt nahīñ! lāibrerī kab band hotī hai?
lines.id: No problem! When does the library close?
lines.literal: any matter not! library when closed becomes?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: آٹھ بجے۔ تو ہمارے پاس ساڑھے تین گھنٹے ہیں۔
lines.baca: āṭh baje. to hamāre pās sāṛhe tīn ghanṭe haiñ.
lines.id: At eight. So we have three and a half hours.
lines.literal: eight o'clock. so our near half-past three hours are.

lines.speaker: عائشہ:
lines.text: کافی ہے۔ جمعرات کو ملتے ہیں!
lines.baca: kāfī hai. jumerāt ko milte haiñ!
lines.id: That's plenty. See you on Thursday!
lines.literal: enough is. Thursday on meet are!

notes: **The phrase ساڑھے چار means 4:30, not 3:30.** Urdu counts **forward**: ساڑھے ("plus a half") is added to the hour that has **already passed**. So ساڑھے چار = "four plus a half" = 4:30. Good news for English speakers: it works just like "half past four". (Learners who know German or Dutch, where "half five" means 4:30, need to watch out.)

**Three time words you have to learn.** The word سوا (*savā*) = a quarter past: سوا چار = 4:15. The word ساڑھے (*sāṛhe*) = half past: ساڑھے چار = 4:30. The word پونے (*paune*) = a quarter to: پونے پانچ = 4:45. Notice that پونے uses the **next** hour — it's the only one that counts backward.

**Two half-hours have their own names.** "One and a half" is **ڈیڑھ** (*ḍeṛh*), not ساڑھے ایک. "Two and a half" is **ڈھائی** (*ḍhāī*), not ساڑھے دو. Only from 3½ on does the regular ساڑھے pattern kick in. These two words are used outside of time too: ڈیڑھ کلو (1.5 kilos), ڈھائی سو (250).

**The always-safe option when in doubt.** Say the minutes in full: **چار بج کر تیس منٹ** ("four having struck, thirty minutes"). It's used at stations, airports, and on the news, so it doesn't sound odd at all — just a little more formal. For "to": پانچ بجنے میں دس منٹ ("ten minutes until five").

**The word بجے means "o'clock" — a point in time, not a duration.** For example پانچ بجے = five o'clock. For a length of time use گھنٹہ, as in پانچ گھنٹے = five hours. Don't mix them up: میں پانچ بجے آتا ہوں ("I come at five") is very different from میں پانچ گھنٹے پڑھتا ہوں ("I study for five hours").

**The word انشاءاللہ ("God willing") attaches to almost every plan.** It isn't doubt but politeness: mentioning a future plan without انشاءاللہ sounds a little overconfident. Answering an arrangement with ٹھیک ہے، انشاءاللہ means "OK, see you then" — and it's the most natural reply.

grammars.title: Telling the time
body: The question is always the same: **کتنے بجے ہیں؟** ("what time is it?") or **کتنے بجے؟** ("what time?", for plans). The answer uses one of the patterns below.

head: Time
Urdu
Say it
Literally
rows: four having struck, then twenty minutes

after: The part of the day goes **in front of** the number, and that replaces a.m./p.m.: صبح کے چھ بجے (6 a.m.), دوپہر کے دو بجے (2 p.m.), شام کے پانچ بجے (5 p.m.), رات کے نو بجے (9 p.m.).
⚠️ Notice بجا for one o'clock and بجے for the rest — because "one" is singular and the others are plural. This small slip doesn't affect meaning, but getting it right makes you sound polished.

grammars.title: Days, months, and time words
body: The Pakistani working week starts on **Monday**, but the most important day is **Friday** — جمعہ — the day of congregational prayers. The weekly days off in Pakistan are Saturday and Sunday.
after: The most common time words: آج (today), کل (**tomorrow and yesterday at once** — only the verb form tells them apart), پرسوں (the day after tomorrow, or the day before yesterday), ابھی (right now), اب (now), بعد میں (later), پہلے (before, earlier).

⚠️ The word کل really does mean two opposite things. میں کل جاؤں گا = "I'll go tomorrow". میں کل گیا = "I went yesterday". Urdu lets the verb decide which way time is pointing — and native speakers are never confused.

blocks.title: Making an appointment in four steps
items: Asking if they're free: آپ کل فارغ ہیں؟ ("are you free tomorrow?") · آپ کے پاس وقت ہے؟ ("do you have time?")
Suggesting a time: ساڑھے چار بجے ٹھیک ہے؟ ("is half past four OK?") · کتنے بجے مناسب ہے؟ ("what time suits you?")
Agreeing: ٹھیک ہے، انشاءاللہ۔ · جی، ضرور۔ ("yes, of course") · مجھے منظور ہے۔ ("that works for me")

Declining gently: معاف کیجیے، اس دن میں مصروف ہوں۔ ("sorry, I'm busy that day") — then **always** offer an alternative: کیا جمعہ کو ممکن ہے؟ Declining without offering another time sounds like you're turning down the person.

ہے / بجے / بند / لائبریری / آٹھ / ہوتی

answers: ساڑھے سات بجے — سوا تین بجے — پونے چھ بجے — ڈیڑھ بجے — ڈھائی بجے
کتنے بجے ہیں؟ — ہم ساڑھے چار بجے ملتے ہیں۔ — میں کل فارغ ہوں۔ — لائبریری آٹھ بجے بند ہوتی ہے۔ — میں آج مصروف ہوں۔
wave: For three days, every time you look at a clock, say the time in Urdu — out loud if you're alone. The one that trips you up most will be پونے.
